Keeping a same-second repeat once keeps the existing two-log dedup, so nothing new is decided.

decisions.summary: T324: task_phases::windows is fixed here so that a stop ends its run, where it had kept an agent's first start for every later stop
decisions.why: This is a defect in another reader of the same stream: a session's own call between an agent's runs was marked as the agent's. It is fixed in this task with a red-first test. That is fixing as we go, not added scope.

decisions.summary: T324: subagent_runs, foreground_spans, feature_report/tables.rs, task_phases::cuts and where_time's walk were each read for repeated starts and stops and are left as they are, or yield each run. stepback_bundle and tool_yield are untouched
decisions.why: The section says what each reader does with repeated lines and finds no wrong outcome. A reader that already behaves correctly has nothing to fix.

decisions.summary: T324: in make task-progress, a resumed builder is RUNNING and one stopped again is stopped at its last stop. decisions.why: This serves T293 ('see while a task is in progress where the time is going'). decisions.summary: T345: from a builder's stop to its next line (and from the line before a start, where no log holds the stop) the builder is STOPPED: a wait on everything it started, with no minutes of its own, so the time leaves the builders' model-turn rows
decisions.why: Amendment (i) makes the percentages 'of the time that our Claude Code sessions spent working', and a stopped builder is not working. The breakdown's existing rule already gives waits blocking and no minutes, as the main session's 'waiting: ...' rows have none. So the 25.6 min the old booking gave as the builder's model turn was a wrong outcome, and removing it is the fix. Amendment (c), 'never a silent other', is met because the time is not dropped unnamed: a reader sees it as blocking on what the stopped builder had in flight, or under the new STOPPED category's blocking, and task-time's footnote says the builder minutes leave the stopped time out.

decisions.summary: T345: one new category, 'builders: stopped, waiting to be resumed' (STOPPED in book/cats.rs), for stopped time with nothing of the builder's own in flight. Where its own run or agent is in flight, the wait is booked to that
decisions.why: Amendment (c) asks for every minute to be named, and the existing names would misstate this time: 'waiting on its background work' says something is running, and 'waiting: nothing in flight' is the main session's and is special-cased in descend. The wording says only what the log shows. Naming a category is within a breakdown the GM asked to be broken down automatically (j).

decisions.summary: T345: a builder is in flight from its first start to its last stop, and its stopped piece is booked through its stop's wait. A review agent between two rounds is not in flight
decisions.why: This applies the per-task, by-dependency blocking definition (l) to a resumed builder. The task does not end while its builder can still be resumed, but a review agent's next round is a new dispatch. No narrowing of the request.

decisions.summary: T345: a stopped builder with nothing of its own in flight is what a wait is on only where nothing else in flight blocks the task (stopped ranked last in each_task and descend). So beside a claims round, the session's wait is on the round

The GM accepted approximation in blocking attribution in (l) ('it doesn't have to be 100% exact'). There is a red-first test with the rank switched off.

blocks: ### T325 (found by 451 T301 part 1, measured 2026-11-26: after a touch of `rust/gate/crates/core`, the 28 gate manifests' test builds ran rustc 75 times for 58 targets, 17 of them a library compiled again under another feature set, `dev/measurements/2026-11-26/cargo-hashes/gate-call.sh`)
### T325 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: The route is the manifests: each crate's [dev-dependencies] names the test-only feature, no cargo call's words change. The task line's two candidates (helpers always compiled; the whole family named in every call) are declined.
decisions.why: The task line is the coordinating session's, not the GM's. It asks for measurement and then the cheaper route, and the plan does that. The command-line route is measured as refused by cargo 1.87 and workspace unification is -Z only. Always-compiled helpers would put test seams into the tools, which the brief forbids. Naming the whole family in every call inflates every builder check. Choosing among routes to the same outcome narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: A crate that is the root names itself with path = "." and its test-only feature (core, research, registry, owed, archive, l7r_shared).
decisions.why: This is an implementation form for the one-feature-set goal and is cargo's own convention. It removes no part of the request.

decisions.summary: The pin computes resolver-2 features from the manifests for the forms the workspace writes, prints the line to add, and does not see or judge a feature named on a command line (counters).
decisions.why: The pin is enforcement of the requested outcome, a test that fails only when a library is compiled under two feature sets. Its blind spot for command-line features does not narrow the outcome: no cargo call's words change, and the touch pass is measured at 58 runs for 58 targets.

decisions.summary: l7r_shared's test-env stays apart: one feature set within the guard's family, not across the workspace, so the library is still built twice in a tree that tests both families.
decisions.why: No GM word asks for one feature set across every family. Unifying test-env would change what 31 crates' tests read (thread map in place of the process environment), which would be a wrong outcome. The leftover is one compile of l7r_shared after an edit of it, a cost and not a wrong outcome, so under constitution XIV it is not a defect left.

decisions.summary: The pin is a test in checks (reads = ["."]), not a new command.
decisions.why: Where the enforcement lives is a design choice and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Accepted: once core and owed resolve with testkit in both clippy passes, the 11 cfg(not(any(test, feature = "testkit"))) production lines are compiled by the tool build and linted by nothing (a seeded len_zero answered 'lint clean'). The choice of mend (a third --lib clippy pass for core and owed, or moving the lines out from under the cfg) is deferred to T389, 'lands before T302'.
decisions.why: This task creates the defect: the block's own seeded lint shows a check answering clean on bad work, and that is a defect under constitution XIV (a check that passes bad work). The GM's standing rule is to fix known defects in the step that finds them, and his approval asked that enforcement be real. None of the three grounds holds. (1) A fix is not impossible: two mends are named. (2) No GM word implies leaving production lines unlinted. (3) Fixing it here does not defeat the task's purpose. The obstacle given for the third pass (it 'brings back' a lib build without testkit, but in check mode, which is not the test-build repeat this task measured and removed) is marked 'not measured'. Moving the lines is given no obstacle at all. 'Which is cheaper is a measurement' is a cost reason, and that measurement can be made in this task. FR-009's form (why, filed id, order) is what make decide checks mechanically; it does not make the deferral legitimate. 'Before T302' cannot be checked from the bundle. The census is also short: the 11 lines come from one literal grep for cfg(not(any(test, feature = "testkit"))). That search misses other spellings (cfg(not(feature = "testkit")), cfg(not(test)) paired with a feature) and the test-env off-branches of l7r_shared, which D2 now has naming itself with that feature, so its own lint pass may have lost reach too. Required: restore lint reach over every testkit-off and test-env-off line in this task (measure the third pass or move the lines), from a census whose search space is stated and covers every cfg spelling. Or show by measurement that no reach was lost.

decisions.summary: The coverage build is resolved with cargo tree for six selections and not compiled. Coverage verdicts, lint over all 34 crates and mode_a's tests are left to the landing's gate.
decisions.why: Under the GM's two tiers of 2026-11-26 (T308), full rigor runs at the landing's gate. This moves where those checks run; it does not reduce what they reach. The resolution evidence covers the requested outcome.

decisions.summary: Two of the pin's three tests exercise code the old tree lacks and were not run red. The main pin was run red (41 lines) and then green.
decisions.why: The test that enforces the outcome was run red first. FR-012's red-first rule covers the refusals of FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013, not this pin. Nothing the GM asked is dropped.

decisions.summary: owed's entry_lines testkit seam is now live in the tests of eight crates that built owed without it.
decisions.why: This is the seam's own documented use. All 28 gate crates' tests ran and passed, so everything works, and a differing test-time path is not a regression (constitution XIII).

decisions.summary: The small lane's key (T347) holds the manifests and the lockfile, so every crate's first build after landing is told wide once. stepped and stale::built are not edited.
decisions.why: This is the existing mechanism working as designed after a manifest edit. Nothing requested is dropped.

decisions.summary: Three rust/Cargo.toml comments that say Cargo.lock is not tracked are left as they are and not filed.
decisions.why: Comment wording with no wrong outcome is not a defect under constitution XIV, and leaving it narrows nothing.

blocks: ### T325 (found by 451 T301 part 1, measured 2026-11-26: after a touch of `rust/gate/crates/core`, the 28 gate manifests' test builds ran rustc 75 times for 58 targets, 17 of them a library compiled again under another feature set, `dev/measurements/2026-11-26/cargo-hashes/gate-call.sh`)
### T325 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: Fix the repeated compiles through the manifests' [dev-dependencies], declining the task line's two candidates (helpers always compiled; whole family named in every call) after measuring that a call-level feature and workspace feature unification are refused or -Z only.
decisions.why: The goal is the one asked: compile less after an edit (the GM's 'more of the compilation was not able to be cached', and FR-013's performance-first). The route is a mechanism, measured rather than assumed; the candidates it declines came from the task line, not the GM, and declining them reduces nothing he asked for - the plan states the cost each would carry (test seams compiled into the tools; one crate's check building all 28).

decisions.summary: A crate that is the root of its build names its own test-only feature in [dev-dependencies] (path = ".").
decisions.why: A mechanism needed for the one-feature-set goal in the crate's own test and coverage builds; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The pin computes resolver-2 feature sets from the manifests and names each short root with the line to add; it does not judge a feature named on a command line (counters).
decisions.why: A test whose only effect is to keep the requested result (one feature set per library) in place - enforcement of what was asked, not new scope. Not seeing command-line features leaves no test-only dev-dependency feature unchecked; counters is not of that kind.

decisions.summary: l7r_shared's test-env is held to one set within the guard's family, not across the workspace; l7r_shared still compiles twice in a tree that tests both families.
decisions.why: Applying the one-feature-set rule literally here would turn test-env on for the 31 gate crates that build on l7r_shared, so their tests would read a thread map where their manifest says they read the process environment - changing what tests check, which defeats the purpose (faster builds of tests that still do their job). The cost left is one extra compile of l7r_shared on an edit of it, not a wrong outcome, so no defect is carried forward; a touch of a gate crate repeats nothing.

decisions.summary: The pin is a test in the checks crate, not a new command.
decisions.why: Placement of the enforcing test; follows the checks/documents precedent and adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: The lint gains a third pass (cargo clippy --lib, no dev-dependencies) for a crate that names itself, so its feature-off lines are linted again.
decisions.why: D2 made both existing lint passes compile with the test-only feature on, leaving the tools' own feature-off lines unlinted (shown with a seeded len_zero passing). The third pass restores the lint's reach the change would otherwise remove - keeping an existing check doing its job, not new scope. Its cost (12.8 s over six crates) is measured and stated beside the saving.

decisions.summary: The coverage build is verified by cargo tree, not compiled; the production builds are verified unchanged by cargo tree diff; the coverage verdicts and full lint are left to the landing's gate.
decisions.why: Verification of the brief's constraints by the routes available to a builder; the gate still runs the full checks. Nothing asked is dropped.

decisions.summary: Eight gate crates' tests now build owed with testkit and so get entry_lines' test seam; all 28 crates' tests pass.
decisions.why: A differing test configuration is not a regression where everything works; the seam is the use owed's own doc comment names, and the tests pass.

decisions.summary: T347's small lane and T336's healed link are left unedited; every crate's first build after landing is told wide once.
decisions.why: Keeps the brief's constraint; the one-time wide build is the ordinary effect of a manifest edit.

decisions.summary: Left unfiled: the pre-warm overlapping the first measurement, three Cargo.toml comments saying the lockfile is untracked, and l7r_shared's two feature sets (D4). T389 is to be withdrawn as mended by D6.
decisions.why: None is a wrong outcome under constitution XIV's definition: the pre-warm is doing its job, the comments' wording changes no outcome and lies outside the task's lines, and D4 is ruled above. T389's work is done by D6, so withdrawing it drops nothing.
